html:
In February 1982 the Syrian army besieged the city of Hama for nearly four weeks to crush an uprising by the Muslim Brotherhood, killing thousands of people, by most estimates between 10,000 and 40,000.

Islamists had waged a campaign of killings against the government of Hafez al-Assad since the late 1970s. When fighters rose in Hama, the army, led by his brother Rifaat, shelled the old city and then went through it house by house. Much of the old centre was destroyed.

For decades Syrians spoke of it only in whispers. Hama is famous for its water wheels. The memory of the massacre came back in 2011, when Hama again filled with protesters at the start of the Syrian civil war.
sum: In February 1982 the Syrian army besieged the city of Hama for nearly four weeks to crush an uprising by the Muslim Brotherhood, killing thousands of people, by most estimates between 10,000 and 40,000.
